summary: Matthew Clark is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London between 1999 and 2004, studying under Daud Ali and George Botterill.
Matthew Immergut works in Buddhist studies and sociology. He studied under Culadasa and was attested in 2011 as an Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Matthew MacKenzie specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1996–2004) and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Colorado State University in 2008.

Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at Duke University under Richard M. Jaffe (attested 2015), also studying at Osaka City University and the IUC.

Matthew T. Kapstein (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After earning a PhD at Brown University (1980–1987), he held posts at Columbia University, the University of Chicago, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Matthew Thomson Adam worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary teacher for the London Missionary Society (1820–1830) and as a teacher at Presidency University until 1830.

Matthew W. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto by 2014 under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

Matthias Alexander Castrén (1813–1852) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki/Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836) and later held posts there from around 1840 to 1852.

Matthias Christian Sprengel (1746–1803) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Rostock, Bützow, and Göttingen (under August Ludwig von Schlözer). He became an extraordinary professor at Göttingen in 1778 and librarian at Halle-Wittenberg (1778–1801).

Matthias Hermanns (1899–1972) was a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at St. Gabriel, Vienna, and Fribourg (PhD 1947–1948). He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954) and the Steyler Missionswissenschaftliches Institut (1960–1968).

Matthias de Vries (1820–1892) was a Dutch linguist. Educated at Leiden University (~1838–1843), he held posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891), and taught Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern.

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Graz, Vienna, Berlin, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD 1859–1860). He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg (1863, 1866), Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard (born 1946) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a doctorate in molecular biology at the Pasteur Institute (1967–1972) before studying under Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, later joining the Mind and Life Institute.

Mattia Salvini specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and has held teaching posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University (attested 2015).

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics. Supervised by B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, he completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University and served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson (1930–2019) worked in Indology, having studied under W. Norman Brown. She served as South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago (attested in 1984 and 2007).

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned degrees from Furman and Johns Hopkins (PhD ~1878–1879 under Charles Rockwell Lanman) and studied across Europe before serving as professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont (1866–1946) was a linguist who studied at EPHE and the University of Paris (PhD 1889–1895). He held posts at the University of Burgundy (1892–1895) and the University of Montpellier as Professor of Comparative Linguistics (1895–1939).

Maurice Jametel (1856–1889) was a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and held a post there from around 1886 to 1889, where he taught Édouard Chavannes.
